title: Prompt flags
summary: Short flags in a message (-d, -w, -nc, -q, -rc, -a, -p, -m, -away) change how Claude handles it.
benefit: One short flag changes how Claude handles a message, without typing instructions.
solves: Typing the same long instructions again and again to steer how Claude handles one message.
use_cases: "-d": discussion only, no edits or state-changing commands.
"-w": search the web first and cite what was found.
"-nc": no commits until you say so.
"-q": Claude asks before acting if anything is unclear.
"-rc": extra rigor: verify end to end, re-run checks, say what could not be verified.
"-a": analyze deeply first: read files, trace logic, weigh options.
"-p": plan mode and a plan for approval, even for a small task.
"-m": keep it for good: a rule goes to CLAUDE.md, a fact to memory.
"-away": leave and let Claude finish alone; "-back" ends it. Both come with the Away mode part.
Put flags at the start or end of a message. They combine and the stricter wins: "fix it -q -nc".
details: Short tokens you put at the start or end of a message change how Claude handles it: -d discussion only, -w search the web first, -nc no commits, -q ask when unclear, -rc extra rigor, -a deep analysis, -p plan mode, -m remember it permanently, plus -away. It is for steering a single message without long instructions. It adds one plain-text rule file under ~/.claude/rules/ that loads into every session; no code runs and no network is used.
trigger: Add a flag such as -d, -w, -q, -rc, -a, -p or -m at the start or end of your message.
risk: Text only, loaded into every session. No code runs.
